title: Superior Versus Inferior Approach to Atrioventricular Node Ablation After Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrioventricular node (AVN) ablation after left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is currently recommended as an effective rate-control strategy in patients with permanent atrial fibrillation, but the exact timing and the optimal venous approach are less standardized.

OBJECTIVE: The current study aimed to compare the feasibility of the superior approach with the standard femoral vein approach for AVN ablation after LBBAP in a single pace-and-ablate procedure.

METHODS: We compared 46 patients with a superior approach and 46 with an inferior approach for AVN ablation after LBBAP based on procedural parameters such as procedural time, fluoroscopy time, ablation time, number of applications, mean power, and temperature.

RESULTS: LBBAP significantly reduced the QRS duration in both groups. Except for a higher R-wave detection in the inferior approach group, all other pacing-related parameters showed no statistically significant differences. The AVN ablation procedure was successful in all patients during the index procedure and from the right atrial side. The total procedural time was significantly shorter with the superior approach. The ablation time, number of applications, mean power, and total fluoroscopy time were similar between the two groups. No periprocedural complications were recorded. The pacing threshold improved in both groups at the 6-months follow-up. One patient in the superior approach group demonstrated recovery of AVN conduction, requiring an additional ablation procedure.

CONCLUSION: As part of a single pace-and-ablate procedure, AVN ablation via the pacemaker pocket had shorter total procedural time and non-significantly different procedural characteristics and outcomes than the standard femoral vein approach.

title: Association between left atrial stiffness index and atrial fibrillation recurrence following radiofrequency ablation
summary: Abstract Background Growing evidence indicates that the left atrial stiffness index (LASI) serves as a straightforward and reliable surrogate for left atrial (LA) function. Although LASI has been linked to atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence, supporting evidence remains limited. Obesity is also implicated in the pathophysiology of AF. Currently, no existing research has investigated the correlation between the Z-score-standardized product of LASI and body mass index (z-LASI-BMI) and AF recurrence. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate the association between z-LASI-BMI and AF recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA). We further evaluated the predictive value of LASI and z-LASI-BMI for post-ablation AF recurrence. Methods In this retrospective study conducted at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Xi’an Jiaotong University, 240 patients who underwent initial RFCA for AF were consecutively enrolled between September 2022 and October 2024. The analysis evaluated the association between left atrial stiffness parameters (LASI and z-LASI-BMI) and post-ablation AF recurrence. Results Over a 12-month observation period post-RFCA, 25.0% of participants exhibited AF recurrence. Multivariable regression analysis confirmed that both LASI and z-LASI-BMI independently predicted AF recurrence. Restricted cubic spline models revealed a positive linear relationship between LASI and z-LASI-BMI and AF recurrence rates. Additionally, adding the z-LASI-BMI index into the fully adjusted baseline risk model significantly improved the prediction of AF recurrence, as reflected by increases in the C-statistic, continuous net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement, but requires external validation. Conclusions Both LASI and z-LASI-BMI were independently associated with AF recurrence after ablation. z-LASI-BMI improved discrimination beyond LASI alone but remains exploratory and requires external validation.

title: Association Between Brain Natriuretic Peptide Level and Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
summary: Background and objectivesPrevious studies suggest a link between brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels and atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the nature of this relationship is disputed. To address this, we conducted a study to gather and assess evidence on the association between BNP and AF.MethodologyStudies were systematically searched and collected from four databases and different types of gray literature. After the screening, the selected articles' quality and risk of bias assessment were evaluated. Meta-analysis calculated std. Mean difference on the extracted data. Furthermore, heterogeneity, sensitivity, subgroups, and publication bias analyses were assessed.ResultsSixteen studies were included in this systematic review. The meta-analysis of 11 studies, comprising 1,418 cases and 3,343 controls, showed a significant and positive association between BNP levels and AF (pooled Std.Mean Difference = 1.08; 95% CI = 0.67, 1.49; P < 0.0001), with no publication bias (P = 0.212). Among the subgroups, significant differences in Std. Mean Differences were observed primarily when stratified by region or risk of bias; however, these analyses were unable to fully account for the observed heterogeneity.ConclusionsElevated BNP levels are strongly associated with prevalent AF. In prospective studies measuring BNP prior to onset, elevated levels served as a modest predictor of incident AF, suggesting its role in identifying underlying atrial myopathy. Further investigations in both molecular and clinical fields with proper methodology and more detailed information are needed to clear the interactive aspects of BNP level in AF patients.

title: Hemorrhagic Cardiac Tamponade in an End-Stage Renal Disease Patient on Apixaban.
summary: Direct oral anticoagulants are used for stroke prevention in selected patients with atrial fibrillation who receive hemodialysis. Randomized trial data remain limited in this population, and the anticoagulant effect of a given dose may vary considerably between patients. We report a 56-year-old man receiving hemodialysis three times weekly who was taking apixaban 5 mg twice daily and developed persistent hypotension and abdominal pain during dialysis. The early findings suggested dialysis-associated hypotension or sepsis. Emergency department point-of-care cardiac ultrasound showed a large circumferential pericardial effusion, leading to urgent cardiology evaluation for obstructive shock. Computed tomography obtained during the same evaluation described the effusion as large and possibly hemorrhagic. Pericardiocentesis was unsuccessful because most of the fluid was posterior. Shortly after transfer to the intensive care unit, the patient developed pulseless electrical activity arrest and underwent an emergent subxiphoid pericardial window. Approximately 450 mL of bloody fluid was drained, followed by hemodynamic improvement. Cytology showed no malignant cells, and fluid cultures were negative. This case also highlights the uncertainty surrounding the use of full-dose apixaban in patients receiving hemodialysis, particularly after a major bleeding event.

title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Incidence, Outcomes, and Treatment.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is the recommended treatment in advanced coronary heart disease. More than 28 000 isolated CABG procedures are performed each year in Germany: almost one-third of patients have transient, new-onset postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) before they are discharged from the hospital. In this narrative review, we outline the detection, incidence, outcomes, and treatment of POAF after CABG on the basis of current evidence.

METHODS: This narrative review is based on guidelines and pertinent publications that were retrieved by a selective search in PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov. In the analysis, randomized controlled trials concerning CABG patients were given priority over observational studies and those involving mixed cardiac surgical cohorts.

RESULTS: Nationwide registries have documented a 30-31% incidence of POAF after CABG, but recent data obtained by continuous monitoring indicate a cumulative 1-year incidence of 48% (95% confidence interval [41; 55]). The atrial fibrillation (AF) burden (time in AF divided by the duration of monitoring) after CABG is low (0.07%), and episodes most commonly arise in the first month after surgery. POAF can be treated acutely with either rate or rhythm control, depending on physician preference. The evidence on long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC) for patients with POAF after CABG is mixed; current data suggest it may not be indicated.

CONCLUSION: POAF often arises shortly after CABG and mainly consists of brief episodes with a low overall atrial fibrillation burden. The role of long-term OAC remains unclear. The guideline recommendations for CABG patients should be reassessed in the light of current evidence.

title: Proton pump inhibitors in antithrombotic therapy: gastroprotection, drug interactions, and clinical management.
summary: Antithrombotic therapy is central to the prevention of thromboembolic and ischaemic events in patients with coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, and after percutaneous coronary intervention, but is accompanied by an increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB). Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) can reduce upper GIB, although their optimal use across different antithrombotic regimens, potential drug interactions, and inability to prevent lower GIB remain clinically relevant concerns. This structured narrative review examines PPI co-therapy in patients receiving antiplatelet agents, oral anticoagulants, or combined antithrombotic treatment. MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 2026, supplemented by contemporary cardiology and gastroenterology guidelines. Randomized trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and large observational studies were prioritized. Evidence indicates that PPIs provide clinically meaningful protection against acid-related upper GIB, particularly in high-risk patients receiving aspirin-containing regimens, dual antiplatelet therapy, or intensified antithrombotic therapy, whereas evidence in isolated oral anticoagulation remains predominantly observational. PPI co-therapy should therefore be targeted according to gastrointestinal bleeding risk and antithrombotic intensity, with periodic reassessment as treatment changes, rather than used as universal gastrointestinal protection. KEY POINTS: • Proton pump inhibitors can reduce the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding in patients receiving antithrombotic therapy, but their benefit is greatest in patients with additional gastrointestinal bleeding risk factors • Their use should therefore be individualized according to gastrointestinal risk and the intensity of antithrombotic treatment rather than prescribed routinely to all patients • The need for gastroprotection should be reassessed whenever the antithrombotic regimen or the patient's bleeding risk changes.

title: Distinct Gut Microbial and Metabolic Biomarkers Related to Atrial Fibrillation in Low-Risk Patients.
Safety, effectiveness and healthcare resource implications of an early discharge pathway for cryoballoon ablation: real-world evidence from China.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Same-day discharge after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation has been increasingly adopted in Western healthcare systems. However, its applicability in China remains uncertain because of differences in healthcare delivery, peri-procedural management, and hospitalization practices. Meanwhile, real-world evidence on early discharge pathways for AF ablation in the Chinese setting remains limited. This study evaluated the clinical and economic outcomes of an early discharge pathway for patients undergoing cryoballoon ablation in China.

METHODS: A retrospective real-world study was conducted using data from the institutional atrial fibrillation database at Fuzhou University Affiliated Provincial Hospital. Consecutive patients who underwent cryoballoon ablation between January 2021 and December 2023 were included. Patients were stratified into two cohorts based on post-operative length of stay: the early discharge (ED) group (discharged within 48 h) and the conventional inpatient (CI) group (discharged after 48 h). Propensity score matching was performed to minimize baseline imbalances between groups. The outcomes were atrial fibrillation recurrence, post-procedural complications and hospitalization cost.

RESULTS: A total of 327 patients were included in the final analysis, with 151 in the ED group and 176 in the CI group. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 80 patients remained in each group, and baseline comparability was substantially improved after matching, although a small residual imbalance remained for stroke/TIA history. During 12 months of follow-up, the recurrence rate of AF was similar between the two groups (8.75% vs. 10.00%, P = 0.786). No major in-hospital complications occurred in the ED group, whereas one case of pericardial effusion was reported in the CI group. Subgroup analyses showed no significant difference in recurrence among patients aged 65 years or older or among those with persistent atrial fibrillation. The ED group incurred significantly lower medical service costs (P = 0.0003) and medication costs (P = 0.035) than the CI group. However, no significant difference was observed in total hospitalization costs between the two groups (P = 0.957).

DISCUSSION: In this real-world Chinese cohort, a structured early discharge pathway for cryoballoon ablation appeared to be feasible and was not associated with a higher AF recurrence rate, while reducing medical service-related costs. However, because this was a retrospective single-center study with a limited sample size and no systematic post-discharge surveillance for all potential events, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Larger prospective studies are needed to further confirm the safety, effectiveness, and economic implications of this model.

title: ECG Holter-based screening for sleep-disordered breathing in post-stroke patients: a large monocentric cohort study.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) is highly prevalent after stroke and is associated with poor functional outcomes and increased mortality, yet systematic screening remains challenging because of limited polysomnography accessibility. We evaluated three electrocardiogram (ECG)-based indices for SDB screening in a large consecutive post-stroke cohort.

METHODS: This retrospective single-centre cohort study included 1,929 consecutive patients hospitalised for stroke or transient ischaemic attack at Saint-Étienne University Hospital (2010-2021) who were in sinus rhythm with ECG signal quality adequate for ECG-derived respiration (EDR) analysis; patients with atrial fibrillation, pacemaker rhythm, or severe ectopy (>10% of beats) were excluded a priori. EDR, the Thoracic Impedance Disturbance Index (TIDI) and the Very Low Frequency Increment (VLFI) were compared with the simultaneous oxygen desaturation index (ODI) as reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, accuracy and predictive values were calculated at ODI thresholds of 15/h and 30/h; a combined TIDI+EDR concordant rule was assessed as a post-hoc exploratory analysis.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 61% males (mean age 65.9 years). Suspected SDB (ODI ≥ 5/h) was present in 74.6% of patients, moderate-to-severe SDB (ODI ≥ 15/h) in 38.9% and severe SDB (ODI ≥ 30/h) in 17.1%. For ODI ≥ 15/h (n = 750), TIDI had the highest sensitivity (93.3%) and negative predictive value (90.8%), whereas EDR had higher specificity (80.2%) and accuracy (74.2%); the combined rule reached 85.2% specificity and 72.9% positive predictive value. For ODI ≥ 30/h (n = 330), EDR showed specificity of 92.4% and accuracy of 85.2%, and the combined rule 95.4% and 86.9%, respectively. VLFI performed poorly across all metrics.

DISCUSSION: ECG-based tools can identify post-stroke patients at high risk of SDB using routine cardiac monitoring. The complementary profiles of TIDI (rule-out) and EDR (rule-in) support a sequential screening approach, which requires prospective validation against polysomnography. VLFI is unsuitable for elderly stroke populations because of age-related autonomic dysfunction. Because patients with atrial fibrillation, pacemaker rhythm or severe arrhythmia were excluded, the findings may not generalise to this higher-arrhythmia-burden subgroup, who may also be at higher risk of SDB.

title: Stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation: radiobiology, clinical evidence, and emerging applications.
summary: STereotactic Arrhythmia Radioablation (STAR) has emerged as a promising non-invasive treatment for patients with refractory cardiac arrhythmias who are unsuitable for or have failed conventional catheter ablation. Initially developed for ventricular tachycardia (VT), STAR has demonstrated encouraging efficacy in reducing arrhythmia burden while avoiding the risks associated with invasive procedures. More recently, limited and early clinical experience has explored the potential application of STAR in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF), including the feasibility of non-invasive pulmonary vein isolation; however, clinical evidence in AF remains anecdotal and investigational. Despite these advances, the biological mechanisms underlying STAR remain incompletely understood. While early hypotheses attributed its therapeutic effects primarily to radiation-induced fibrosis, accumulating evidence suggests that rapid anti-arrhythmic effects are mediated by early electrophysiological reprogramming and conduction remodeling, whereas delayed vascular injury, inflammation, and fibrosis may contribute to durable substrate modification and long-term toxicity. This evolving paradigm has important implications for optimizing radiation dose, fractionation strategies, and minimizing cardiac toxicity. Advances in imaging, electroanatomical mapping, and treatment planning are further improving treatment precision. Ongoing prospective clinical trials and international collaborative initiatives are expected to provide robust evidence regarding efficacy, safety, and long-term outcomes. This review summarizes current knowledge on the radiobiological mechanisms, clinical applications, and future perspectives of STAR, highlighting the key challenges for its integration into contemporary cardiac electrophysiology, as well as describing our current clinical trial investigating the role of dose and fractionation for this technique.

title: Preventive Linear Ablation Strategy for Intra-Atrial Reentrant Tachycardia Following Cardiac Surgery.
summary:
AIMS: Intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia (IART) frequently occurs following cardiac surgery due to scar-related conduction abnormalities. While advances in mapping technologies have improved the acute success rate of catheter ablation, arrhythmia recurrence remains a significant clinical concern. This study aimed to evaluate whether a preventive linear ablation strategy guided by voltage mapping improves the long-term success rate of catheter ablation in patients with IART post-cardiac surgery.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 46 consecutive patients following cardiac surgery who underwent atrial tachycardia ablation between 2022 and 2024 were enrolled in the study group. After activation mapping-guided ablation for ongoing IART, preventive linear ablation was performed based on voltage mapping. Fifty consecutive sex- and age-matched patients with cardiac surgery undergoing activation mapping-guided ablation alone served as the historical control group between 2018 and 2021. At a mean follow-up of 21 ± 4.9 months, the rate of freedom from atrial arrhythmias was significantly higher in the study group compared to the control group (82.6% vs. 64.0%; p = 0.019). Despite the improved outcomes, the study group had significantly longer total procedure times (192 ± 37 vs. 126 ± 25 min; p < 0.001) and radiofrequency ablation durations (29 ± 5 vs. 20 ± 6 min; p < 0.001). However, there were no significant differences in complication rates between the two groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Preventive linear ablation strategy was associated with improved arrhythmia-free survival in patients with IART post cardiac surgery, but these exploratory findings require confirmation in future prospective studies.

title: Impedance-Based Contact Visualization for PulseSelect Pulmonary Vein Isolation: A Single-Center Feasibility Study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: PulseSelect pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) lacks a dedicated contact indicator.

METHODS: We retrospectively compared 63 patients undergoing PVI before and after EnSite Contact Index (CI) implementation. Because electrical isolation does not confirm lesion transmurality, post-procedural unipolar electrograms (u-EGMs) were assessed as acute surrogate markers.

RESULTS: CI guidance was associated with more applications, shorter fluoroscopy, and in an exploratory analysis of analyzable patients, fewer residual high-voltage u-EGMs (1/20 vs. 8/24; p = 0.027). No complications occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: CI-guided PVI was feasible; these procedural and acute electrophysiological associations require prospective validation.

title: Contemporary Outcomes of Catheter Ablation of Long-Standing Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Advances in mapping and ablation have improved the safety and efficacy of catheter-based ablation (CA) of atrial fibrillation (AF). Patients with long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation (LSPAF) historically have poor ablation outcomes; however, they are underrepresented in contemporary reports.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate ablation approaches and long-term rhythm control following contemporary catheter ablation for LSPAF.

METHODS: A single-center, retrospective analysis of patients undergoing CA for LSPAF between 2021 and 2025 was performed. Demographic and procedural characteristics were analyzed; 1-year arrhythmia free survival and atrial arrhythmia burden were assessed.

RESULTS: Ninety-five patients (median age 68 years [IQR, 63-73]; 80% male; median BMI 32.4 kg/m2 [IQR, 28.6-35.6]; median ejection fraction 55% [IQR, 49%-60%]; 37% with prior CA) were followed for a median of 20.2 months (IQR, 10.2-29.7). Radiofrequency ablation alone was used in 74 patients (78%), pulsed-field ablation alone in 13 (14%), and both in 8 (8%). Pulmonary veins were isolated in all patients, 88 (93%) underwent additional left atrial ablation, including linear ablation in 88 (93%), posterior wall isolation or ablation in 72 (76%), vein of Marshall ethanol infusion or ablation in 25 (26%), coronary sinus ablation in 24 (25%), and cavotricuspid isthmus ablation in 23 (24%). Fourteen of 92 post-blanking evaluable patients (15.2%) were receiving a class I or III antiarrhythmic drug at last follow-up. Among 57 patients with adequate post-blanking follow-up after a first AF ablation (of 60 first-ablation patients overall), 1-year arrhythmia-free survival was 39.3% (95% CI, 27.8%-55.4%). Among all patients and after allowing repeat procedures, 1-year arrhythmia-free survival was 53.5% (95% CI, 43.3%-66.1%). Among patients with continuous monitoring, median arrhythmia burden decreased from 90.1% (IQR, 21.1%-99.4%) before ablation to 0.0% (IQR, 0.0%-3.8%) at 6 months and 0.0% (IQR, 0.0%-20.0%) at 12 months.

CONCLUSION: In this contemporary cohort of patients undergoing CA for LSPAF, 1-year arrhythmia-free survival was 53.5% when repeat procedures were allowed. Among patients with implanted cardiac devices, arrhythmia burden was markedly reduced after ablation and may complement conventional time-to-first-recurrence endpoints.

title: True Left-Ventricular Aneurysm After Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation: The Role of Imaging in a Rare Complication.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular (LV) pseudoaneurysm is an uncommon but recognized complication of ventricular tachycardia (VT) ablation. In contrast, true LV aneurysm has been reported only rarely.

CASE SUMMARY: Transthoracic echocardiogram, supported by cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging, initially suggested an LV pseudoaneurysm in a patient after VT ablation. During evaluation for percutaneous closure, left ventriculogram and 3-dimensional transesophageal echocardiogram revealed more complex anatomy, prompting referral for surgical repair. Intraoperative findings confirmed a true LV aneurysm.

DISCUSSION: True LV aneurysm may represent a rare complication of deep radiofrequency energy delivery during catheter ablation resulting in myocardial injury. Because differentiating true aneurysms from pseudoaneurysms can be challenging, a multimodality imaging approach may improve anatomical characterization, guide management, and enhance understanding of the underlying mechanism.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Multimodality imaging can improve anatomical characterization and procedural planning in patients with the rare complication of true left aneurysm after catheter ablation.

title: Arrhythmia management in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
summary: Arrhythmias are common in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and contribute substantially to morbidity at all disease stages. The arrhythmogenic substrate-reflecting diffuse amyloid infiltration, atrial myopathy, autonomic dysfunction, and conduction system involvement-differs fundamentally from that in other cardiomyopathies. Prospective rhythm monitoring reveals a burden substantially higher than previously recognised and predominantly asymptomatic, with bradyarrhythmias and atrial fibrillation (AF) dominating and sustained ventricular arrhythmias remaining rare.This review examines key aspects of arrhythmia management in ATTR-CM. Conduction system disease is frequently encountered, and pacing strategies-including conduction system pacing-are discussed in the context of progressive infiltrative disease. We address the rationale for lifelong anticoagulation in AF irrespective of CHA2DS2-VA-score, and emerging considerations for anticoagulation in selected sinus rhythm patients with impaired atrial function. Rhythm control strategies are reviewed in light of extensive atrial substrate, high AF recurrence rates, and the absence of randomised trial data. The role of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators is examined, with emphasis on the lack of proven survival benefit for primary prevention. Finally, we explore disease-modifying therapies and their potential to attenuate the arrhythmogenic substrate. Overall, structured surveillance, rhythm control, and individualised device decisions form the cornerstones of modern arrhythmia management in ATTR-CM.

title: Prevalence of thyroid dysfunction in patients with acute atrial fibrillation attending coronary care unit at Al-Sadder Teaching Hospital.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: Aim: Assessment of prevalence of thyroid dysfunction in patients with acute atrial fibrillation.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Materials and Methods: A total of 110 patients participated in this cross-sectional study, admitted to the coronary care unit with AF not more than 48 hours from symptom onset and investigated by TSH, T3, and T4 to show how prevalent thyroid dysfunction in patients with acute AF, a study done at Al-Sadr Medical City - Najaf Al-Ashraf city, Iraq.

RESULTS: Results: This study showed Prevalence of thyroid dysfunction was 21.7% which represents 24 patients that include (one patient with subclinical hypothyroidism 0.9%, 4 patients with subclinical hyperthyroidism 3.6%, 5 patients with hypothyroidism 4.5%, 14 patients with hyperthyroidism 12.7% and patients with euthyroid represent (N=86, 78.3%) of patients.

CONCLUSION: Conclusions: For patients who admitted to the coronary care unit with acute atrial fibrillation both hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism were frequent with the latest exceeding the prevalence in the general population necessitating screening for hidden thyroid dysfunction for early diagnosis and management to reduce morbidity and mortality.

title: Beyond HAS-BLED in very elderly patients with atrial fibrillation treated with direct oral anticoagulants: predictors of major bleeding in a real-world cohort.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Bleeding risk assessment in very elderly patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) remains challenging. The HAS-BLED score is widely used but may have limited applicability in this population. We aimed to evaluate its performance and to identify clinical predictors of major bleeding beyond conventional risk scores.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective real-world cohort study including consecutive patients aged ≥ 90 years with AF treated with DOACs. The primary outcome was major bleeding. Discrimination was assessed using receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify predictors and assess incremental value.

RESULTS: A total of 487 patients (mean age 93.0 ± 2.6 years, 63.4% female) were included, with major bleeding occurring in 57 patients (11.7%). The HAS-BLED score was not associated with major bleeding (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.55-1.23; p = 0.34) and showed poor discrimination (AUC 0.46). In multivariable analysis, increasing age (OR 1.14 per year, 95% CI 1.03-1.27; p = 0.014) and anticoagulant type were independently associated with bleeding. Compared with apixaban, rivaroxaban (OR 3.77, p = 0.002) and dabigatran (OR 3.34, p = 0.008) were associated with higher bleeding risk. A clinical model incorporating these factors modestly improved discrimination compared with HAS-BLED (AUC 0.69 vs. 0.46).

CONCLUSIONS: In very elderly patients with AF receiving DOAC therapy, HAS-BLED has limited predictive value. Bleeding risk appears to be influenced by treatment-related factors, particularly anticoagulant type. Incorporating these factors may improve risk stratification and support a more individualized approach to anticoagulation management in nonagenarians.

title: Association of coronary artery calcium with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation according to atrial fibrillation type.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) reflects systemic atherosclerosis and inflammation and may contribute to atrial remodeling. Although CAC has been associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF), whether this association differs according to AF type remains unclear.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 202 consecutive patients who underwent first-time catheter ablation for AF and had coronary computed tomography between October 2019 and August 2024. CAC was quantified using the Agatston score. The primary outcome was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond a 90-day blanking period. Patients were stratified by AF type, and associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Branch-specific CAC was also evaluated in exploratory analyses. During a median follow-up of 617 days (IQR, 457-808), atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 19 of 96 patients with paroxysmal AF (PAF; 19.8%) and 39 of 106 patients with non-PAF (36.8%). In the overall cohort, CAC ≥100 was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after adjustment for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and left atrial volume index (adjusted HR, 2.03; 95% CI, 1.07-3.86; P=0.031). In age- and sex-adjusted analyses stratified by AF type, CAC ≥100 was associated with a higher risk of recurrence in patients with PAF (adjusted HR, 5.59; 95% CI, 2.05-15.27; P<0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in patients with non-PAF (adjusted HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.56-2.52; P=0.647). The interaction between CAC ≥100 and AF type was statistically significant in the age- and sex-adjusted model (P for interaction=0.011) and remained significant in the expanded clinically adjusted model including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and left atrial volume index (P for interaction=0.005).

CONCLUSIONS: CAC ≥100 was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after AF ablation, and this association may differ according to AF type, with a stronger association observed in patients with PAF. Subgroup and interaction analyses were exploratory and limited by the small number of recurrence events. CAC may provide useful information for post-ablation recurrence risk stratification, although these findings require validation in larger prospective studies.

title: Cardiac arrest associated with standard-dose carvedilol in combination with amiodarone: a case report.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Patients with cardiac and metabolic comorbidities often undergo procedural intervention as well as pharmacological management. Medication adjustment is made in anticipation of and/or as a response to procedures. We present a case where failure to track and verify pre- versus post-procedural doses of a commonly prescribed medication led to substantial morbidity. This report emphasizes the need for vigilance even when using medications generally considered safe and for enhanced information sharing across different electronic medical record systems.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 61-year-old Hispanic man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and recent direct current cardioversion (DCCV) for new-onset atrial fibrillation was readmitted to the hospital for dyspnea. He had been recently discharged from the hospital for atrial fibrillation after being cardioverted to normal sinus rhythm. He was maintained, however, on carvedilol 25 mg twice daily-the same dose prescribed to him prior to DCCV-resulting in bradycardia, relative hypotension, acute kidney and liver injury. A few months later, at an elective admission at another hospital, he underwent ablation for refractory atrial fibrillation and was inappropriately restarted on the previous carvedilol dose; subsequently he had bradycardia and two Pulseless electrical activity (PEA) arrests.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights that intolerance to Atrioventricular (AV)-nodal blockade and Bradycardia, Renal failure, AV nodal blockade, Shock, and Hyperkalemia (BRASH) physiology can occur at standard dosing, particularly with drug interactions and hemodynamic vulnerability. It underscores the importance of rigorous medication reconciliation, anticipatory de-escalation of rate-controlling agents after rhythm-control procedures, and improved cross-system access to prior adverse drug events. In the long term, individualized precision medicine may reduce adverse reactions to widely used medications at commonly prescribed doses.

title: [Importance of ventricular extrasystole coupling intervals for risk stratification].
summary: The importance of measuring the coupling intervals of ventricular extrasystoles is discussed, with practical diagnostic, prognostic and therapeutic application in various clinical situations: risk stratification of malignant ventricular arrhythmia and sudden death in cases with short and long coupling interval of ventricular extrasystoles; diagnosis of a variety of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with repercussions in the therapeutic decision to be made; risk stratification of ventricular tachycardia of the right ventricular outflow tract, benign and malignant forms; localization of the origin of ventricular extrasystoles and risk stratification of sudden death in ischemic heart disease and heart failure.

title: Transient Type 1 Brugada ECG Pattern in a Patient With Severe Coronary Artery Disease.
summary: A type 1 Brugada electrocardiographic (ECG) pattern is characteristic of Brugada syndrome but may also occur in association with reversible clinical conditions, including myocardial ischaemia. We describe a 49-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, severe hypercholesterolaemia and a strong family history of premature ischaemic heart disease who presented with crescendo angina. His admission ECG demonstrated a type 1 Brugada pattern, with subsequent ECGs showing dynamic anterior ischaemic changes. Coronary angiography demonstrated extensive multivessel coronary artery disease, and the patient underwent urgent surgical revascularisation following Heart Team discussion. Serial postoperative ECGs demonstrated complete resolution of the type 1 pattern despite continuation of his regular medication, including mirtazapine. In the absence of arrhythmic syncope, documented ventricular arrhythmia, previous cardiac arrest or a family history of sudden cardiac death, sodium-channel blocker provocation testing was not pursued. Although latent Brugada syndrome cannot be definitively excluded, the temporal relationship between myocardial ischaemia, revascularisation and ECG normalisation supports an ischaemia-associated Brugada phenotype.

title: Early ambulatory re-evaluation and follow-up of patients admitted in the acute cardiac care unit - Practical aspects on ambulatory follow-up of acute care patients: acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias, atrial arrhythmias, conductance disorders, myocarditis, pericarditis, other acute cardiac settings A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care of the ESC.
summary: Early, structured ambulatory follow-up after hospitalization for acute cardiac events remains a key unmet need in cardiovascular care. This clinical consensus statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care of the ESC provides pragmatic, condition-specific guidance on post discharge management and (early) ambulatory re-evaluation for patients admitted to an acute cardiac care unit. It complements existing disease-oriented guidelines by focusing on the vulnerable transition from hospital to home rather than on acute in-hospital treatment. The document first defines key concepts and outlines general principles regarding timing, content, and organization of the first post-discharge contacts, including risk stratification, medication reconciliation, symptom assessment, evaluation of psychosocial status and comorbidities, patient and family education, and integration of cardiac rehabilitation. In practice, the consensus statement discusses the patient's path after discharge: how should the follow-up team look like, when should the first and subsequent visits be planned, what should be done at each contact, and how can multidisciplinary teams and hybrid (in-person plus remote) models be implemented according to local resources. Supplementary material highlights major evidence gaps, including the optimal timing and intensity of follow-up, the composition of ambulatory teams, the role of telemonitoring and digital health, and the needs of vulnerable populations. Overall, this consensus aims to support clinicians in designing structured, individualized, and scalable ambulatory pathways after acute cardiac care.
journal: Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care

title: Associations of ECG-derived markers with clinical and biological characteristics in systemic sclerosis: preliminary findings from the SCAR-SSc study.
summary: Cardiac involvement in systemic sclerosis (SSc) is often subclinical in its early stages. Electrocardiographic markers have been associated with arrhythmias and myocardial remodeling and may provide insight into cardiac involvement in SSc. This pilot single-center cross-sectional study explored associations between ECG-derived parameters and clinical and biological features in patients with SSc without overt cardiovascular disease. Thirty-four patients meeting the 2013 American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology classification criteria were included. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and high-sensitivity troponin I were measured, standard 12-lead ECGs were analyzed for interatrial block (IAB), morphology-voltage-P-wave duration (MVP) score and fragmented QRS (fQRS), and 24-hour Holter monitoring was used to quantify arrhythmias. Participants were 85.3% women, with a median (IQR) age of 53.6 (46-61) years and disease duration of 7.95 (1.5-14.8) years; 76.5% had limited cutaneous SSc. Fragmented QRS was present in 7 of 32 patients with evaluable fQRS data (21.9%), and its presence was associated with a higher premature ventricular contraction count on Holter monitoring after adjustment for age and sex (OR = 1.0022; 95% CI, 1.0001-1.0044; P = 0.044). Partial IAB was present in 4 of 8 patients (50%) with diffuse cutaneous SSc. The modified Rodnan skin score (mRSS) differed between patients with and without IAB (9 ± 9 versus 3 ± 4, P = 0.040). Higher MVP scores were associated with mRSS (β = 0.422, P = 0.026), C-reactive protein (β = 0.412, P = 0.028) and NT-proBNP (β = 0.557, P = 0.003). ECG-derived markers were associated with measures of disease severity, ventricular ectopy and NT-proBNP levels. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger studies.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Omecamtiv Mecarbil by QRS Duration and Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy in GALACTIC-HF.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged QRS duration portends worse outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). In GALACTIC-HF, omecamtiv mecarbil (OM) reduced the primary composite endpoint of first heart failure (HF) event or cardiovascular death.

OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to evaluate whether QRS duration and the presence of cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) modify the treatment effect of OM.

METHODS: GALACTIC-HF enrolled patients with symptomatic HF, HFrEF (≤35%), and elevated natriuretic peptides. Baseline QRS duration was available in 8,089 of 8,232 participants (98.0%), who were classified into 3 groups: QRS duration <120 ms without CRT (n = 3,724), QRS duration ≥120 ms without CRT (n = 3,225), and CRT regardless of QRS duration (n = 1,140). The authors assessed whether the effect of OM on the primary composite endpoint, first HF hospitalization, cardiovascular death, and all-cause death differed across these groups.

RESULTS: Patients with QRS ≥120 ms without CRT and those with CRT were older, had lower EF, worse health status, and higher N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels than those with QRS <120 ms without CRT. When modeled as a continuous variable, baseline QRS duration was associated with clinical outcomes among patients without CRT but not among those with CRT. Among patients with QRS ≥120 ms without CRT, OM appeared to confer less benefit for the primary composite endpoint (Pinteraction = 0.072), for cardiovascular death (Pinteraction = 0.003), and for all-cause death (Pinteraction = 0.009). In contrast, among patients treated with CRT, OM was beneficial regardless of QRS duration.

CONCLUSIONS: In GALACTIC-HF, OM appeared less effective in patients with prolonged QRS duration who did not have CRT, whereas it remained beneficial in CRT-treated patients. (Global Approach to Lowering Adverse Cardiac Outcomes Through Improving Contractility in Heart Failure [GALACTIC-HF]; NCT02929329).

title: Peri-procedural immune blood cell count changes and pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an exploratory study.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a minimally invasive treatment for aortic stenosis. Although significant advancements in the TAVI technique have been made, the risk of requiring a permanent pacemaker remains clinically relevant.

AIM: The aim of the study was to analyze the relationship between peri-procedural blood count parameters and the risk of pacemaker implantation after TAVI.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: The retrospective study analyzed 115 patients (median (Q1-Q3) age of 76.7 (73.5-81.9) years). Demographic and clinical data were collected. The counts of leukocytes, neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, and platelets were assessed before the procedure, on the day of the procedure (8 hours after the procedure), 24, 48, and 72 hours after the procedure, and at hospital discharge. Pre-procedural and post-procedural heart rhythm disturbances have been recorded.

RESULTS: The analysis showed a predominant increase in neutrophil and monocyte counts after the procedure, without differences between subgroups. Moreover, a decrease in lymphocyte counts was observed after TAVI; however, it was less pronounced in patients who required pacemaker implantation. Patients without heart rhythm disturbances experienced a greater decrease in their lymphocyte count. In the multivariable analysis, an increase in lymphocyte count after the procedure was an independent factor for pacemaker implantation (OR = 5.2, 95% CI: 1.6-16.3, p = 0.005).

CONCLUSIONS: After TAVI, increases in neutrophil and monocyte counts and decreases in lymphocyte counts are observed; however, the lymphocyte count decrease is less pronounced in patients with heart rhythm disturbances requiring pacemaker implantation. An increase in lymphocyte count after the procedure was independently associated with pacemaker implantation.

title: [Myocardial fibrosis and ventricular tachycardia in myotonic dystrophy type 1].
summary: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 is a neuromuscular disorder associated with an increased risk of arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death, for which risk stratification remains a clinical challenge. We report the case of a 45-year-old woman with genetically confirmed myotonic dystrophy type 1 who presented with palpitations and dyspnea. Electrocardiography revealed sinus bradycardia and first-degree atrioventricular block, while Holter monitoring demonstrated a high burden of premature ventricular complexes and episodes of both non-sustained and sustained ventricular tachycardia. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed late gadolinium enhancement involving 29% of the left ventricular mass, with a non-ischemic intramyocardial and subepicardial pattern consistent with extensive myocardial fibrosis. Based on the overall arrhythmic risk profile, an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted for primary prevention. During follow-up, no syncope, ventricular arrhythmias, or device therapies were documented. This case highlights the value of a multimodal approach to optimize arrhythmic risk stratification and guide individualized management.

title: Enhanced prediction and risk stratification of atrial fibrillation with polygenic risk score in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes
authors: The Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank Study Group
summary: Abstract Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common adverse outcome in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D); however, the role of genetics in identifying those at risk of AF within this high-risk group have not been comprehensively studied. Methods A total of 20,009 individuals from two prospective cohorts of Chinese patients with T2D were analyzed. We calculated a polygenic risk score (PRS AF ) comprising 97 variants previously associated with AF risk. Associations of PRS AF with incident AF and other cardiovascular endpoints were assessed using Cox regression, adjusted for baseline covariates. We also determined whether adding PRS AF improved prediction compared to the CHARGE-AF score using C-index, net reclassification improvement index, and integrated discrimination improvement index. Results Incident AF occurred in 986 patients (5.1%) across the two cohorts. A higher PRS AF , adjusted for sex, age, duration of diabetes, and principal components, was associated with increased risks of incident AF (HR [95% CI] per SD = 1.42 [1.33–1.51]), stroke (1.07 [1.01–1.12]), and congestive heart failure (1.10 [1.04–1.17]). These associations remained significant in the fully adjusted model. Patients in the top PRS AF quintile were over 2.5-fold (95% CI = 2.08–3.17) as likely to develop AF than those in the bottom quintile. A novel risk score that integrates the PRS AF into the CHARGE-AF score significantly improved both discrimination and reclassification compared to the CHARGE-AF score alone. Conclusions In patients with T2D, PRS AF is an independent risk factor for AF, providing incremental value in prediction and risk stratification, beyond that achieved with a validated clinical risk score.

title: Transforming cardiac amyloidosis care: navigating the evolving diagnostic and therapeutic landscape.
summary: Amyloidosis comprises a group of systemic disorders caused by extracellular deposition of misfolded precursor proteins, leading to progressive organ dysfunction. Cardiac amyloidosis, particularly transthyretin-related amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) has transitioned from a rare and underdiagnosed condition to a treatable disease, driven by major advances in diagnostic imaging, increased disease awareness, and the approval of disease-modifying therapies. These therapies target transthyretin (TTR) stabilization and amyloid production or deposition and have led to an evolving therapeutic landscape. As therapeutic efficacy is greatest in earlier disease stages, timely recognition is crucial. Effective management of ATTR-CM requires structured screening of high-risk populations, multidisciplinary collaboration, and longitudinal follow-up. This review provides a practical, clinician-focused framework that addresses clinical presentation and "red flags" to facilitate early detection. It offers a comprehensive overview of the diagnostic pathway, including (AI-enabled) electrocardiography analysis, (non-)invasive imaging modalities, biomarkers, and genetic testing. Additionally, emerging therapeutic strategies are discussed, encompassing supportive heart failure management, amyloid-specific treatments such as TTR stabilizers and gene silencers, and novel approaches including fibril depletion and gene-editing therapies. As the therapeutic paradigm shifts from disease stabilization toward potential reversal, early diagnosis and personalized treatment strategies are essential to improve prognosis and quality of life in patients with cardiac amyloidosis.

title: Molecular profiling uncovers KCa2.3 as key driver of pacemaker cells in glioblastoma.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Glioblastoma is orchestrated by pacemaker cancer cells, a rare population preferentially residing at the hubs of tumor cell networks. These cells autonomously generate periodic Ca2+ oscillations that drive glioblastoma network function, resilience, and disease progression. To date, the Ca2+-activated K+ channel KCa3.1 is the only known driver of pacemaker function, calling for studies to identify additional factors - to better understand a key component of glioblastoma pathobiology, and uncover novel therapeutic targets.

METHODS: A molecular Ca2+ integrator technology enabled the transcriptional profiling of highly Ca2+-active glioblastoma cells, a population enriched for pacemaker cells. Putative regulators of pacemaker function were interrogated using genetic, pharmacological, and computational approaches across complementary glioblastoma models.

RESULTS: We identified a distinct transcriptional program that captures highly Ca2+ active glioblastoma cells, including pacemaker cells, across preclinical models and human glioblastoma specimens. This program comprised upregulated cholesterol biosynthesis enzymes, TM-network markers (Aquaporin-4 and Cystatin C), and the Ca2+-activated K+ channels KCa1.1 and KCa2.3. Amongst these components, in silico modeling identified KCa2.3 as the only channel compatible with executing pacemaker function. Consistently, KCa2.3 expression was increased in pacemaker cells, and both genetic and pharmacological perturbation of KCa2.3 selectively disrupted pacemaker function, resulting in reduced network-wide Ca2+ activity. Ultimately, pharmacological inhibition of KCa2.3 with edelfosine reduced tumor burden in human brain spheroids.

CONCLUSIONS: We present the first experimental approach to characterize molecular factors of glioblastoma pacemaker cells in a broad and unbiased manner, and identify KCa2.3 as a novel pacemaker gene and promising therapeutic target.

title: Long Term Outcomes of Pediatric Patients After Catheter Ablation for Possible Arrhythmia Induced Cardiomyopathy.
summary: Arrhythmia induced cardiomyopathy (AiCM) is reversible, and catheter ablation has become the standard treatment for most arrhythmias. However, as the diagnosis of AiCM can be made only in retrospect, management is often challenging. A single center retrospective study included patients who had ablation for presumed AiCM after January 2011 to assess the outcomes of ablation, and the final diagnosis. 22 patients (11 female) were included in the study with the following distribution of arrhythmias: Atrial Ectopic Tachycardia (AET) = 8, Permanent Junctional Reciprocating Tachycardia (PJRT) = 6, Ventricular Tachycardia = 3, Premature Ventricular Contraction = 1, Atrial Flutter = 1, Atrioventricular Reciprocating Tachycardia = 1. There were two patients where an EP study did not show a specific arrhythmia substrate and the patients proceeded in the transplantation pathway. Of the 20 patients with confirmed tachycardia, four (20%) had complete normalization of function with+ medical management. The remaining 16 patients (80%) achieved no or partial functional recovery, with ablation playing even more important role in these patients. One AET patient showed no recovery of function despite successful ablation, consequently requiring heart transplant due to later confirmed gene-positive cardiomyopathy. Overall, 19 patients (95%) showed normal cardiac function at the end of study period with diagnosis of AiCM. There was one significant complication with AV block due to RF ablation on ECMO in a newborn with PJRT. While medical management can achieve functional recovery in some pediatric AiCM cases, most patients will require catheter ablation with 88% success rate. However, once functional recovery is achieved, long term outcome is excellent. Very rarely ventricular function will not recover despite successful ablation as genetic cardiomyopathies can present with secondary arrhythmia.

title: Single-nucleus transcriptomic analysis identifies a putative Purkinje fiber-associated remodeling program after myocardial infarction.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Purkinje fiber (PF) remodeling may contribute to post-infarction ventricular arrhythmia, but rare conduction-associated cardiomyocyte states in injured human myocardium remain incompletely characterized. We use TsPF to denote transitional PFs, a study-specific transitional Purkinje fiber subpopulation resolved by cardiomyocyte re-clustering and characterized by an intermediate transcriptional phenotype. In this study, transitional refers to the observed expression phenotype; temporal progression, lineage conversion, and anatomical Purkinje localization require separate evidence.

METHODS: We performed a secondary analysis of the human myocardial infarction atlas reported by Kuppe et al. The analyzed discovery matrix was derived from 29 single-nucleus RNA-sequencing libraries representing 28 tissue specimens from 20 individuals (4 donor controls and 16 individuals with myocardial infarction). After quality control and Seurat/Harmony integration, ventricular cardiomyocytes were re-clustered. PF/TsPF annotation, MiloR, high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA), scMetabolism, PF-anchored pseudotime, and CellChat were evaluated with an explicit separation between abundance testing, descriptive molecular patterns, and model-derived hypotheses.

RESULTS: The quality-controlled matrix contained 172,522 nuclei and 28,122 genes. All MiloR neighborhoods had a spatial false discovery rate (SpatialFDR) of at least 0.05. A secondary tissue-sample-level TsPF: mature-PF ratio was lower in myocardial infarction than control in the displayed comparison (unadjusted Wilcoxon P = 0.0345); several tissues came from the same donors, and mature-PF denotes the PF-labeled denominator. Using β = 5, hdWGCNA resolved nine colored modules; the selected blue module contained 1,050 genes, including NT5C, ITPA, GUK1, and ADSS1. TsPF-labeled nuclei showed higher nucleotide-metabolism scores (average log2 fold change = 0.9982; Bonferroni-type adjusted P = 4.63 × 10 - 27; cell-level comparison). CellChat network summaries showed 1,191 versus 805 inferred interactions and aggregate strength 0.095 versus 0.027 in control versus myocardial infarction; these values are descriptive model outputs rather than donor-level differential tests.

CONCLUSIONS: This secondary analysis prioritizes a putative PF-associated transcriptional remodeling program for follow-up. The abundance result remained negative after SpatialFDR correction, while the co-expression, metabolic, ordering, and communication analyses provide candidates for hypothesis-driven work. Establishing a distinct TsPF state and its functional relevance will require independent donor-aware, spatial/histological, molecular, and electrophysiological validation.

title: Long-term outcomes of intermuscular versus subcutaneous S-ICD implantation: extended follow-up of a propensity-matched multicentre analysis.
Design and Validation of a Custom-Made Electrocardiogram Machine for Low-Cost, High-Fidelity Cardiac Monitoring.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: Electrocardiography (ECG) is an essential diagnostic tool in cardiovascular medicine; however, access remains limited in low-resource settings because of cost and infrastructure requirements. This study aimed to develop and preliminarily validate a low-cost, custom-made ECG device capable of real-time cardiac monitoring and arrhythmia detection.

METHOD: A portable ECG system incorporating a low-noise analog front-end, microcontroller-based digital processing, and Bluetooth-enabled wireless transmission was designed. Preliminary validation was performed using simultaneous recordings from one healthy volunteer and three patients with documented cardiac arrhythmias, and the results were compared with those of a commercial ECG system in terms of signal quality and rhythm interpretation.

RESULTS: The custom-made device provided stable real-time ECG recordings with satisfactory signal fidelity and low noise levels. Comparative analysis demonstrated encouraging agreement with the commercial ECG system in waveform morphology and arrhythmia identification. Wireless data transmission was reliable throughout the recordings.

CONCLUSION: This pilot proof-of-concept study demonstrates the technical feasibility of a low-cost, custom-made ECG system for real-time rhythm monitoring and preliminary detection of selected cardiac arrhythmias. The device showed satisfactory signal fidelity and agreement with a commercial ECG system in a small validation cohort. Larger prospective studies are required to establish diagnostic accuracy, reproducibility, and clinical generalizability.
